elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “EITHER PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes fees paid or payable.
elements.evidence: The cap includes “TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID OR PAYABLE FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb measures the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause refers to the “IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD” but does not identify the claim, or any other event, as the reference point for that period.

elements.element: The cap includes a USD 1,000,000 limb.
elements.evidence: The second limb is expressly “USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The operative language expressly uses “THE GREATER OF (A) ... AND (B) USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion of indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no exclusion of consequential damages.

elements.element: Each party's breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: “EXCLUDED CLAIMS,” which are excepted from the cap, include a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Each party's breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's breach of its data protection obligations.

elements.element: Each party's breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's breach of its security obligations.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include “A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 12.”

elements.element: Each party's gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Each party's wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's “WILLFUL MISCONDUCT,” which is equivalent to wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Each party's fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's fraud.

elements.element: Each party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Client's obligation to pay compensation due under Section 5 “SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.”

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The cap applies to “EITHER PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY.”

elements.element: The mutual liability cap equals 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, not a cap equal to 12 months' fees; the 12-month period also lacks an express reference-point trigger.

elements.element: Each party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's indemnification obligations under Section 12.

elements.element: Each party's breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations.

elements.element: Each party's gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's gross negligence.

elements.element: Each party's wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include a party's willful misconduct.

result.reason: The redline adds most preferred cap mechanics and carve-outs, but it omits the required mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages and fails to anchor the 12-month lookback to the claim. It also does not meet the fallback's exact 12-month-fees cap because the operative cap is the greater of that amount and USD 1,000,000. In addition, moving the limitation paragraph after an indemnity lead-in ending with a colon unnecessarily interrupts that provision's syntax and may impair the existing indemnity structure, so the redline is neither minimal nor reliably intent-preserving.
